title: One foot out: Understanding Bulgaria’s geopolitical shift under Radev – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: ECFR's policy alert documents Bulgaria agreeing to host up to eight US refuelling tankers at Bezmer just days after withdrawing from the European coalition of the willing for Ukraine, and argues Rumen Radev is trading European security commitments for bilateral US security guarantees — a hedging model other European governments may copy as the Trump administration conducts foreign policy through bargaining.

insights.claim: Bulgaria has agreed to host up to eight American refuelling tankers at its Bezmer military base to support US operations in the Middle East, announced just days after prime minister Rumen Radev withdrew the country from the European coalition of the willing for Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Maria Simeonova, Vessela Tcherneva
insights.so_what: A concrete, datable case of a member state substituting a US bilateral arrangement for a European commitment — the template to watch elsewhere in the EU.

insights.claim: Radev justified exiting the coalition of the willing by arguing military support would only prolong the war and that Bulgaria lacks the resources to contribute, while simultaneously offering logistical support for American military operations elsewhere.
insights.speaker: Maria Simeonova, Vessela Tcherneva
insights.so_what: The resource-scarcity argument is selectively applied, which reveals the underlying choice is strategic alignment, not capacity.
insights.locator: The announcement came just days after

insights.claim: Radev put the final Bezmer decision to a parliamentary vote to spread political responsibility and limit direct ownership of the move, allowing him to preserve US security guarantees without committing Bulgaria to Europe's developing security architecture.
insights.speaker: Maria Simeonova, Vessela Tcherneva
insights.so_what: Procedural risk-transfer to parliament is the tell for a leader who expects domestic blowback — a signal that the policy lacks confident political backing.
insights.quote: Radev has put the final decision on Bezmer to a vote in Bulgaria’s parliament, allowing him to spread the political responsibility and limit direct ownership of the move.
insights.locator: Radev has put the final decision on Bezmer

insights.claim: Radev is not aligning with the broadly pro-European consensus and anti-American sentiments in Bulgarian society, but instead balancing competing security frameworks without sufficiently considering European security interests.
insights.speaker: Maria Simeonova, Vessela Tcherneva
insights.so_what: Policy is running against domestic opinion, which makes it reversible with a change of government or sufficient EU pressure.
insights.locator: Rather than aligning with the broadly pro-European consensus

insights.claim: As the Trump administration continues to conduct foreign policy through bargaining, some European governments appear tempted to pursue bilateral arrangements with Washington rather than invest in European unity, which risks weakening collective defence precisely when strategic coordination is needed.
insights.speaker: Maria Simeonova, Vessela Tcherneva
insights.so_what: The core second-order effect of transactional US diplomacy is EU fragmentation — a structural headwind for European defence-industrial consolidation.
insights.quote: Such behaviour risks weakening collective defence, precisely when strategic coordination is needed.
insights.locator: This ambiguity also presents a broader challenge

insights.claim: The previous deployment of as many as 15 US tanker aircraft at Sofia Airport between February and June was linked to arrangements for discussions on Bulgaria's inclusion in the US Visa Waiver Program, which were unsuccessful, and the government ended that deployment on 30 June.
insights.speaker: Maria Simeonova, Vessela Tcherneva
insights.so_what: Basing access was explicitly traded for a consular concession and the trade failed — a documented price point for what US bilateral bargaining actually delivers.
insights.locator: The latest move in Bezmer follows

insights.claim: Bulgaria's drift is cumulative: since taking office in May 2026 Radev has not joined the international agreement establishing the Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine and did not attend May's B9 summit in Bucharest.
insights.speaker: Maria Simeonova, Vessela Tcherneva
entities: Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression
insights.so_what: A pattern of repeated abstentions in under three months — track further absences from B9 and EU security formats as the leading indicator.

insights.claim: Bulgaria's recent work to delist two Russian oligarchs and a Russian patriarch from the EU's 21st sanctions package is cited as evidence of Russia's growing leverage over the government in Sofia.
insights.speaker: Maria Simeonova, Vessela Tcherneva
insights.so_what: Sanctions-list carve-outs are the most concrete measurable form of external capture inside EU decision-making — worth monitoring package by package.
insights.locator: Bulgaria’s recent work to delist two Russian oligarchs

insights.claim: Delays in military modernisation and uncertainty around planned defence-industrial cooperation including a Rheinmetall partnership are compounding Sofia's lack of clarity about whether it intends to be a consistent contributor to Europe's security architecture.
insights.speaker: Maria Simeonova, Vessela Tcherneva
insights.so_what: A named commercial exposure: Rheinmetall's Bulgarian partnership is a live casualty of Sofia's strategic ambiguity.

insights.claim: The authors argue the EU should reinforce political and practical incentives for participation in common defence initiatives through the Multiannual Financial Framework and other European defence instruments, and reduce opportunities for China, Russia and the US to exploit divisions and the strategic ambiguity encouraged by MAGA.
insights.speaker: Maria Simeonova, Vessela Tcherneva
insights.so_what: MFF conditionality is the proposed enforcement mechanism — a route by which EU budget design becomes a defence-policy instrument.
insights.quote: European security cannot rely on member states choosing cooperation only when politically convenient.

insights.claim: The EU should treat Bulgaria as an urgent political case rather than a lost cause, because in 2027 several major European elections could return governments more concerned with nationalism than European unity, constraining the space in which pro-European governments can act.
insights.speaker: Maria Simeonova, Vessela Tcherneva
insights.so_what: 2027 is the stated deadline before which the political room for European security integration narrows — the same window flagged across ECFR's 2026 enlargement work.
insights.quote: Overall, the EU should treat Bulgaria as an urgent political case rather than a lost cause.
